# ezghcloud_cdn_distribution_waf (Resource)

Attaches a WAF to a CDN distribution, where it inspects every request before the origin. A distribution has at most one WAF; destroying this detaches it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Inspect every request to the distribution before it reaches the origin.
resource "ezghcloud_cdn_distribution_waf" "web" {
  project_id      = var.project_id
  distribution_id = ezghcloud_cdn_distribution.web.id
  waf_id          = ezghcloud_waf.web.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `distribution_id` (String) Distribution (cdn_). Changing it replaces the attachment.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the distribution and the WAF. Changing it replaces the attachment.
- `waf_id` (String) WAF (waf_) in the same project. Changing it switches the distribution to the other WAF in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The distribution's ID (cdn_).
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `status` (String) deploying until every location enforces the WAF's latest version, then active; failed when one couldn't. Apply doesn't wait for it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_cdn_distribution_waf.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/cdn_ID'
```
